2. It is the case of the applicants that respondent No.2 has lodged an FIR in crime No.45/2023 for offence under Section 498-A, 323, 294, 34 of IPC on the allegations that she got married to applicant No.3 on 16/01/2020 as per the social rituals.
After her marriage, she resided in her matrimonial house for 2-3 days.
Thereafter she came back to Gurgaon along with her husband.
Applicant No.3 as well as respondent No.2 were serving at Gurgaon.
For some days, the things moved properly but from 08/04/2020 applicant No.3 started quarrelling with NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26526 her on trivial issues.
He always used to say that respondent No.2 should say sorry to him.
Whenever she said sorry, it was responded by applicant No.3 that he is of the view that the word sorry has not been said from her heart.

When she used to cry on account of abnormal behavior of applicant No.3, then applicant No.3 used to quarrel with her and used to dash his head against the wall and used to cause injuries to himself by picking up the Deepan Kumar Hastir vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111297269/

sentences.text: She used to get afraid from the behavior of her husband.

She informed the abnormal behavior of her husband to applicants No.1 and 2 but they used to convince her that respondent No.2 must say sorry to applicant No.3 and handle him because he must be under stress because of over work load.

Since respondent No.2 was not interested to spoil her marital life,
therefore for lot of time she tolerated the things but behavior of applicant No.3 did not change.

During this period, applicants No.1 and 2 also resided with them at Gurgaon and even in front of them applicant No.3 had picked up quarrel with her and by causing injuries to himself he compelled the respondent No.2 to say sorry but applicants No.1 and 2 used to support her husband and they were always suggesting respondent No.2 to adjust.

Whenever respondent No.2 suggested that applicant No.3 must be suffering from some mental problem, therefore he should be treated for the same, then applicant No.1 & 2 always insisted that the applicant No.3 is not suffering from any mental problem.
In the year 2021, they both i.e. respondent No.2 and applicant No.3 suffered from COVID-19 Virus, therefore they went to Shimla on 24/04/2021 where they resided for about one year.
Even during their stay at Shimla, behavior of applicant No.3 was same.

When respondent No.2 informed her parents about the abnormal behavior of applicant No.3 then they expressed their NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26526 willingness to visit Shimla but they were not allowed by applicants No.1 & 2.
After one year, applicant No.3 as well as respondent No.2 came back to Gurgaon.
On 04/11/2023 at about 6 PM, applicant No.3 as well as respondent No.2 went to see fair and she was talking to applicant No.2 on mobile phone because she was not well.
Applicant No.3 tried to hide behind the mob.
When respondent No.2 requested him to move then he did not come.

When she informed her husband that she had located him, then he started abusing her filthily in front of entire mob and he insisted that she should say sorry to him and again stated that she is not saying sorry from bottom of her heart and pushed her.
When she tried to go towards the Car, then applicant No.3 came running and caught hold of her neck and pushed her.
As a result, she sustained injury on the elbow of right hand.

Thereafter applicant No.3 called applicants No.1 & 2 on phone and requested them to come immediately and to obtain divorce from respondent No.2 because he is tolerating her for the long time and she always creates seen in front of general public.
Thereafter she narrated the incident to her parents and on the next date i.e. 05/11/2023, applicants No.1 and 2 came to their house at Gurgaon.

When the entire behavior of applicant No.3 was narrated to applicant No.2, then again she stated that since applicant No.3 is under pressure of work load,
therefore she should adjust.
At about 12:30, her parents also came to Gurgaon and they tried to talk to applicants No.1 & 2 but applicant No.1 did not respond, whereas applicant No.3 did not come out of room.
Even applicant no.2 did not accept that applicant no.3 is at fault and all the time was suggesting the mother of respondent no.2 that the entire fault is of respondent no.2.
When she came out of the house along with her parents to come back along with them to her parental NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26526 home, then it was video-graphed by applicant no.3
Thereafter, she came to Ratlam and since then, she is staying at her parental home.
Accordingly, it is claimed that on account of physical and mental cruelty committed by applicants no.1 to 3, legal action be taken against them.

3. Challenging the FIR and registration of offence, it is submitted by counsel for applicants that if the entire FIR is read, then it is clear that except making an allegation that applicant nos.1 and 2 had supported their son, no other allegation has been made against them.

Admittedly, applicants no.1 and 2 are the residents of Shimla, whereas applicant no.3 was residing along with respondent no.2 Deepan Kumar Hastir vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111297269/
2 in Gurgaon.

sentences.text: All the allegations with regard to abnormal behaviour are against applicant no.3.
No allegation has been made against respondents no.1 and 2 to prima facie show that they had in any manner committed cruelty on respondent no.2.

4. None for respondent no.2 though served and represented.
5.

Per contra, counsel for the State also stated that except the allegations of supporting applicant no.3, there are no allegations against applicants no.1 and 2 of committing cruelty with respondent no.2.

6. Heard learned counsel for parties.
7.
This Court has already reproduced the FIR containing allegations against applicants no.1 and 2.
Applicants no.1 and 2 are the resident of Shimla.
There is no allegation that they ever treated respondent no.2 with cruelty.

The only allegation is that whenever a complaint with regard to abnormal behaviour of applicant no.3 was made to applicants no.1 and 2, then they always suggested respondent no.2 to adjust and did not try to get applicant no.3 treated for mental problem.
By no NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26526 stretch of imagination such an allegation can be said to be cruelty as defined under Section 498-A of IPC.

There are no allegation of making any physical assault by applicants no.1 and 2.
8.

Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that in absence of any material to indicate that applicants no.1 and 2 had committed any offence, registration of FIR No.45/2023 at Police Station Mahila Thana Ratlam, District Ratlam for offence under Sections 498- A, 323, 294, 34 of IPC was bad in law.
9.

Accordingly, FIR in Crime No.45/2023 registered at Police Station Mahila Thana Ratlam, District Ratlam for offence under Sections 498-A, 323, 294, 34 of IPC qua applicant No.1 - Deepan Kumar Hastir and applicant No.2 - Gargi Hastir is hereby quashed.

10. So far as registration of offence against applicant no.3 is concerned, there are specific allegations against applicant no.3 of committing cruelty with respondent no.2.
11.

Section 498-A of IPC reads as under:-
498A. Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.-

Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.

Explanation.--For the purposes of this section, "cruelty means"--
(a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether Deepan Kumar Hastir vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111297269/
3 mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:26526 harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.
12.

sentences.text: Thus, any act of the husband which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman, would amount to cruelty.

13. Considering the allegations made against applicant no.3, it is held that the FIR prima facie makes out an offence against applicant no.3.
14.
Accordingly, application filed by applicant no.3-Gaurav Sharma for quashment of the FIR is hereby rejected.
15. Thus, this application qua Deepan Kumar Hastir and Gargi Hastir is allowed, whereas this application qua Gaurav Sharma is hereby rejected.

(G.S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE Arun*
